web_title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside the $16 Billion Engine — Specialty Pharmacy, LTC & Home Health
question: How does BrightSpring generate ~$12.9 billion in FY2025 (and ~$16.0 billion guided FY2026) revenue across Pharmacy Solutions and Provider Services, and what does a real-world patient episode look like in each segment?

epigraph.quote: Our third quarter results again reflect the commitment of our team to patient care and operational execution across our Pharmacy and Provider businesses... supported by a broad set of process and growth drivers across a uniquely scaled and high-quality platform.
epigraph.author: Jon Rousseau, CEO, BrightSpring Health Services (Q3 2026 Earnings Release)

web_blocks.title: 2.1 Segment Architecture & Revenue/EBITDA Mix (Post-Community Living Divestiture)

web_blocks.html: Following the March 30, 2026 sale of ResCare Community Living, BrightSpring reports two continuing segments: Pharmacy Solutions and Provider Services [1, 2]. Community Living is now classified as discontinued operations [1, 2]. In FY2025, consolidated continuing revenue reached $12,910.6 million, up 28.2% year-over-year [1, 3]. Adjusted EBITDA totaled $617.6 million, up 34.2% year-over-year [1, 3]. By Q3 2026, annualized revenue had passed $16.8 billion [2]. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $15.9–$16.125 billion and Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $850–$860 million [2].

Pharmacy Solutions is the main top-line and profit engine. It generated 88.7% of FY2025 consolidated revenue, or ~$11.45 billion (+30.7% YoY) [1, 3]. The segment has two sub-lines. First, Infusion and Specialty Pharmacy makes up ~70.5% of consolidated revenue (~$9.1 billion in FY2025) [3]. It is led by Onco360 in oncology and CareMed in rare and chronic disease, alongside home infusion [3, 9]. Second, Home and Community Pharmacy accounts for ~18.2% of consolidated revenue (~$2.35 billion in FY2025) [3]. Anchored by PharMerica, it serves skilled nursing, assisted living, and behavioral health sites [3, 9]. In Q3 2026, Pharmacy Solutions posted $3.7 billion in revenue (+26% YoY), driven by 34% growth in Specialty and Infusion [2].

Provider Services contributes 11.3% of FY2025 consolidated revenue, or ~$1.46 billion (+11.1% YoY) [1, 3]. It delivers clinical care directly in homes and communities [1, 3]. Core lines include Home Health Care & Hospice, which averaged ~31,135 daily patients in FY2025 [3]. Average daily census surged 58% year-over-year in Q3 2026 after BrightSpring integrated 107 Amedisys and LHC branches [2, 8]. The segment also runs Rehabilitation Care (~7,127 persons served) and Personal Care (~16,079 persons served) [3]. In Q2 2026, Provider Services revenue rose 30% year-over-year to $466 million [4].

web_blocks.takeaway: Infusion & Specialty Pharmacy already accounts for 70.5% of revenue and is growing >30% annually, while Provider Services delivers higher-margin clinical care (~11.3% of sales, ~28% of segment EBITDA) [2, 3].

web_blocks.title: 2.2 Concrete End-to-End Examples Across Every Operating Line

web_blocks.html: Example 1 — Pharmacy Solutions (Specialty Oncology via Onco360): Picture a patient newly diagnosed with Stage IV lung cancer or neurofibromatosis type 1. The doctor prescribes a new targeted oral kinase inhibitor that carries strict Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) rules [9]. The drug is restricted to a Limited Distribution Drug (LDD) panel of just 3 to 5 national pharmacies [9]. When the oncologist sends the e-prescription to Onco360, the Louisville hub begins 'Total Protocol Management' [9]. Staff verify medical and pharmacy benefits, file prior authorizations, and enroll the patient in copay or foundation grants [9]. A board-certified oncology pharmacist checks for drug interactions and ships temperature-controlled pills overnight [9]. Those high-dollar scripts lifted consolidated pharmacy revenue per script to $263.93 in FY2025 [3]. They also support manufacturer data fees and dispensing gross profit of $28.86 per script by Q3 2026 [2, 3, 9].

Example 2 — Pharmacy Solutions (Home & Community LTC via PharMerica): Consider an 82-year-old skilled nursing facility (SNF) resident recovering from hip surgery with diabetes and heart failure. Instead of managing twelve retail bottles, PharMerica's regional closed-door pharmacy links straight to the facility's electronic health record [3, 9]. Staff pack daily doses into barcode-verified multi-dose blister packs or unit-dose strips [3, 9]. Consultant pharmacists review regimens monthly to catch adverse drug events [3, 9]. Regional couriers deliver scheduled refills plus 24/7 stat emergency kits [3, 9]. Gross profit per script is tighter here than in oncology. The line also absorbed a -$50 million Medicare Part D IRA pricing reset in Q1 2026 [4]. Still, PharMerica's dense route network locks in sticky facility contracts [4, 9].

Example 3 — Provider Services (Home Health & Infusion / Rehab): Imagine a 74-year-old Medicare patient discharged home after septic knee surgery. The patient needs six weeks of intravenous antibiotics and physical therapy. BrightSpring's Adoration Home Health branch coordinates the hospital discharge, potentially from one of the 107 acquired Amedisys/LHC sites [2, 8]. A skilled nurse visits the home for IV care and wound checks [2, 8]. In-home physical therapists help restore mobility, while BrightSpring's infusion pharmacy compounds and ships the IV drug [2, 8]. Keeping the patient out of a $2,500-a-day hospital bed or $500-a-day SNF bed saves payers money [2, 8]. That alignment drives steady referrals from Medicare and managed-care plans [2, 8].

web_blocks.title: 2.3 Revenue Mix vs. Profit Mix & Cross-Segment Referral Synergy

web_blocks.html: Judging BrightSpring by revenue mix alone hides where cash profits actually come from [1, 3]. Specialty oncology and rare-disease therapies carry high wholesale drug costs [1, 3]. Those pass-through prices pushed consolidated pharmacy revenue per script to $263.93 in FY2025, up 26.1% year-over-year [1, 3]. As a result, Pharmacy Solutions makes up 88.7% of revenue at an optical gross margin near 10% to 12% [1, 3]. Provider Services has minimal drug pass-through cost and converts clinical labor into higher EBITDA margins [3]. In Q4 2025, Pharmacy Solutions earned $162 million in segment EBITDA while Provider Services earned $64 million [3]. Provider Services thus delivered ~28% of combined segment EBITDA on just ~11.3% of sales [3].

Operationally, both segments reinforce each other at hospital discharge and during chronic care [2, 8]. Complex patients leaving acute hospitals often need both compounded home infusions and skilled nursing visits [2, 8]. BrightSpring's home health and hospice network now spans ~30 states [2, 8]. It served 31,135 average daily patients in FY2025 and grew ADC 58% year-over-year in Q3 2026 [2, 3]. That reach lets BrightSpring capture both medication and clinical-care referrals as a single post-acute partner [2, 3, 8]. Meanwhile, Rehab Without Walls (~7,127 persons served) and Personal Care (~16,079 persons served) extend care into neuro-rehab and daily support [3]. Those services deepen ties with local hospitals and Medicare Advantage plans [2, 3, 8].

book_paragraphs: If you only glance at BrightSpring's revenue split, it looks like a pure drug distributor. Pharmacy Solutions supplies 88.7% of its $12.9 billion in FY2025 continuing sales ($11,452 million). Provider Services supplies only 11.3% ($1,459 million). That top-line ratio is misleading because specialty drug prices are huge while service labor is smaller per episode. Look one layer deeper at gross profit and segment EBITDA. In Q4 2025, Pharmacy Solutions generated $162 million in segment EBITDA, while Provider Services generated $64 million. Provider Services punches nearly three times above its revenue weight, contributing ~28% of segment EBITDA on just over a tenth of sales.

Let's walk through how those businesses work on the ground, starting with Onco360 and CareMed. Together, they anchor Pharmacy Solutions' $9.1 billion Infusion and Specialty sub-line, or 70.5% of consolidated sales. Picture a patient in Ohio newly diagnosed with Stage IV lung cancer or a rare genetic disorder. The doctor prescribes a new oral kinase inhibitor that costs $15,000 a month and carries strict FDA REMS rules. The drugmaker does not send that pill to a corner retail chain. Instead, it limits distribution to a Limited Distribution Drug (LDD) panel of three to five elite specialty pharmacies.

When the oncologist sends that e-prescription to Onco360's Louisville hub, the real work starts before a pill ships. A dedicated team runs 'Total Protocol Management.' Staff verify whether the drug falls under the medical or pharmacy benefit and file prior authorizations. They also secure manufacturer copay cards or charity grants so the patient won't abandon care over a $2,000 out-of-pocket bill. Next, an oncology pharmacist checks drug interactions, counsels the patient 24/7 on side effects, and ships temperature-controlled doses overnight. That clinical service lifted pharmacy revenue per script 26.1% to $263.93 in FY2025. It also raised pharmacy gross profit per script 21.4% to $21.64 in FY2025 and 27% to $28.86 in Q3 2026.

Now contrast that oncology hub with PharMerica, the Home and Community Pharmacy unit at 18.2% of revenue (~$2.35 billion in FY2025). Picture an 82-year-old nursing-home resident recovering from hip surgery with diabetes and heart failure. Instead of juggling twelve retail bottles, PharMerica's closed-door pharmacy plugs directly into the facility's electronic health record. Staff pack daily doses into barcode-verified blister packs or automated unit-dose strips. Consultant pharmacists review drug regimens monthly, while couriers deliver scheduled refills and 24/7 stat emergency kits. It is sticky infrastructure, yet government pricing pressure bites hardest here. In Q1 2026 alone, Medicare Part D changes under the Inflation Reduction Act cut roughly $50 million from Home and Community revenue, prompting management to exit uneconomic contracts.

Finally, step inside Provider Services—home health, hospice, neuro-rehab (~7,127 patients), and personal care (~16,079 patients). In late 2025, BrightSpring paid $239 million for 107 Amedisys and LHC Group branches. That deal nearly doubled its home health footprint from 14 states to roughly 30. It also drove Q3 2026 average daily census up 58% year-over-year from a FY2025 base of ~31,135 patients. Picture a 74-year-old Medicare patient sent home after septic knee surgery who needs six weeks of IV antibiotics and physical therapy. Instead of staying in a $2,500-a-day hospital bed or $500-a-day nursing home, a BrightSpring Adoration nurse visits the home. The nurse handles wound care and IV lines while BrightSpring's infusion pharmacy compounds and delivers the antibiotics.

Why does this two-segment model work better together than apart? Complex post-acute patients rarely need just a pill or just a nurse. A patient leaving the hospital with a severe infection, brain injury, or late-stage cancer often needs both sterile infusion compounding and skilled nursing visits. Pharmacy Solutions brings massive top-line scale, reaching $3.7 billion in Q3 2026 (+26% YoY) on 34% growth in Specialty and Infusion. Meanwhile, Provider Services anchors local hospital discharge ties across 30 states and generates high-margin clinical EBITDA ($466 million revenue in Q2 2026, up 30% YoY). Pairing $9.1 billion of fast-growing Specialty Pharmacy with a surging home-health census creates a balanced post-acute flywheel. As CEO Jon Rousseau noted in Q3 2026, the company relies on 'a broad set of process and growth drivers across a uniquely scaled and high-quality platform.'

Let's also trace a real-world Rehab Without Walls and Personal Care episode so those smaller units don't get overlooked. Picture a forty-five-year-old patient recovering from a traumatic brain injury or stroke after hospital discharge. Instead of staying in a sub-acute rehab facility far from family, Rehab Without Walls sends occupational, physical, and speech therapists into the home. Therapists train the patient to climb stairs, manage daily routines, and regain independence. Meanwhile, Personal Care aides help roughly 16,079 people nationwide with bathing, meals, and medication reminders. Those services lack the headline size of a $15,000 oncology script, yet they deepen ties with state Medicaid plans and Medicare Advantage coordinators.

Keep that contrast in mind whenever you read a BrightSpring earnings release. If you only check consolidated gross margin (~11.8% in FY2025), you will misread the business. Every new $15,000 oncology script at Onco360 inflates revenue and pulls percentage gross margin down, even while adding $28.86+ of gross profit dollars. Watch the two-engine dashboard instead. Track Infusion and Specialty revenue growth (+34% YoY in Q3 2026) alongside Provider Services census growth (+58% YoY in Q3 2026) and Adjusted EBITDA scaling toward $850–$860 million in FY2026.

book_callouts.title: Revenue Mix vs. Profit Mix
book_callouts.text: High-ticket specialty drugs inflate top-line revenue ($263.93 per script in FY2025) and compress optical gross margins (~11.8%). Never judge a specialty pharmacy by its percentage gross margin alone—watch gross profit dollars per script ($21.64 in FY25 -> $28.86 in Q3 26) alongside Provider Services' higher-margin clinical EBITDA.
